newsitem.title: CHINA: HK people fear no spread of Macau gang violence.
newsitem.headline: HK people fear no spread of Macau gang violence.

text.p: Most Hong Kong residents believe that they will remain safe from the violent triad gang wars that have rocked nearby Macau, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday.
The poll by the Apple Daily newspaper showed 49.4 percent of the sample of 332 people surveyed said they were not worried about the spread of violence.
But 41.3 percent of respondents said they were worried and 9.3 percent said they did not know, the newspaper said.

Portuguese-administered Macau has been caught in a crossfire between secret criminal societies, or triads. This week a homemade bomb was hurled at the Macau Government Palace, gunmen opened fire in the grounds of a hotel, and two cars were set ablaze.
The hotel was the scene of two bomb attacks earlier this month.
Police have linked the mayhem to triad gang wars over casino-related protection and loansharking rackets.

Triads operate in Hong Kong, Macau and southern China with tentacles that stretch to Chinese communities around the world. They are often well organised and linked to illegal activities ranging from drug trafficking, smuggling and prostitution to protection rackets.
